section_1.title: The Learning Objective: Meet Sparky
section_1.content: Introduce the goal of neural network learning through a relatable character. Define learning as the process of adjusting internal parameters to reduce mistakes.
section_1.example: Sparky the Robot is trying to distinguish between an 'Apple' and a 'Lemon'. Currently, he keeps calling lemons 'Apples'. We need to teach him by adjusting his internal 'brain' dials.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Forward Pass (Signal Flow)
section_2.content: Explain how data moves from input to output. Visualize weights as 'volume knobs' on wires that amplify or dampen signals.
section_2.example: Visual: An image of a lemon passes through wires. Each wire has a knob (Weight). If the 'Yellow' wire knob is turned up high, the signal for 'Lemon' should be stronger at the end.

section_3.title: The Cost Function: Measuring the 'Ouch'
section_3.content: Introduce the mathematical concept of a 'Loss Function'. It calculates the distance between the prediction and the actual truth. Higher loss means a bigger mistake.
section_3.example: Sparky predicts 90% Apple for a Lemon. The 'Sadness Meter' (Loss) spikes to a high value. Visually, this is shown as a bar chart comparing the 'Prediction' bar to the 'Truth' bar.

section_4.title: Intuitive Backpropagation: The Chain of Blame
section_4.content: Explain Backpropagation as tracing the error backward. We ask: 'How much did this specific knob contribute to the Sadness Meter?' Use the Chain Rule visually as a series of proportional dependencies.
section_4.example: Animation: The 'Sadness' signal travels backward from the output. We see the wires glow red. If a specific weight knob was turned way up and caused the wrong answer, it glows brightest—this knob deserves the most 'blame' (Gradient).

section_5.title: Gradient Descent: The Nudge
section_5.content: Introduce the Gradient as a compass pointing 'uphill' toward more error. Learning means stepping in the opposite direction (downhill). Explain the 'Learning Rate' as the size of the step.
section_5.example: Sparky looks at the 'blame' assigned to a knob. If the gradient says 'Turning this up increases error,' Sparky nudges the knob slightly down. We see a ball rolling down a 3D valley toward the lowest point of error.

section_6.title: The Iterative Loop: Practice Makes Perfect
section_6.content: Summarize how repeating Forward Pass -> Loss -> Backprop -> Gradient Descent leads to 'intelligence'.
section_6.example: Show a montage of Sparky seeing 100 lemons. With every backprop step, his knobs align perfectly. Finally, a lemon appears, and Sparky confidently shouts 'Lemon!' with 0% Loss.

Learning means adjusting these dials to fix mistakes.
